prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper): intake/triage/dispatch/coordination; preserve reports/clarifications, confirmed/estimated distinctions; escalate readiness gaps; record authorization time/unit-selection rationale; maintain coverage from positions/crew/readiness; produce Unit Staging Change Card. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur): verify/repeat location before medical details; capture callback/demographics/symptoms/onset/hazards/barriers/source; produce Caller Location Correction Slip; resolve/update before dispatch. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield): prioritize threats/time-sensitivity/deterioration/delay-harm; reassess, resolve disagreements/document rationale; clarify without delaying urgency; confirm response level; send Pediatric Acuity Note. Regional Medical Director: policy/delegation/consultation, no dispatch authority. Data Quality Officer: audit defects/priority/rationale; no independent clinical-priority changes. Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates incidents/assignments/positions/status/capabilities/coverage/access. Computer Aided Dispatch Console presents current authorized incident/priority/availability/travel/access/staging information; staff verify currency. Dispatcher selects by confirmed priority/needs/travel/capability/readiness/coverage; regional authorization rules apply. Shift Commander (Sundial): continuity/surge/conflicts; approve coverage-reducing/nonstandard exceptions; review coverage before staging moves; escalate jurisdictionally, never override clinical authority. Radio Coordinator (Mistral): verify talkgroup availability/reachability/backups; transmit identifier/location/priority/assignment/hazards through Regional Radio Network; retry absent acknowledgment, alert dispatch supervisor; send Coverage Gap Bulletin below threshold; confirm approved route changes before diversion. Dispatcher retransmits discrepancies; state confirmed gate constraints/uncertainty. Controlled handoff requires crew acknowledgment and dispatch confirmation. Paramedic Crew: protocol/scope care; acknowledge/repeat location/priority; promptly report condition/barrier/readiness/status changes and route conflicts. Ambulance Unit 417: follow assignments/request safety clarification; report staging-entry/exit position/status; remain until dispatch confirms relocation/response. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay): defects/restrictions; verify clearance before availability; Battery Swap Voucher authorizes replacement. Hospital Liaison Desk (Kestrel): destination/capacity/compatibility/constraints without intake delay; coordinate receiving Emergency Department; Bedside Arrival Receipt confirms arrival. Riverside Trauma Center: suitability/availability/guidance. North Gate Status Board: access/queues, North Approach Queue Snapshot. South Gate Status Board: southern access/restrictions; both

New part:
S137: Shift Commander sends the Mutual Aid Release Form when a neighboring service is released from regional coverage.
S138: Regional Dispatch Center uses the swap voucher to confirm that a unit's battery readiness is current before it is placed in service.
S139: Regional Dispatch Center uses the queue snapshot to account for congestion approaching the northern entry before assigning a route.
S140: North Gate Status Board displays the latest queue condition and access restriction for units approaching the northern entry.
S141: Triage Supervisor advises dispatch when changes in clinical demand may require repositioning available units.
S142: Regional Medical Director establishes clinical priorities that dispatch applies when assigning units during elevated demand.
S143: Hospital Liaison Desk provides receiving-facility capacity information for consideration during transport planning.
S144: Dispatchers compare projected response times with remaining coverage before moving a unit away from its current area.
S145: Data Quality Officer reviews inconsistent location or status reports and routes corrections through the established operational process.
S146: Ambulance Coordination Platform retains time-stamped status changes so supervisors can review the sequence of unit movement.
S147: A crew advises dispatch when a road closure, unsafe condition, or unexpected delay makes the assigned route unsuitable.
S148: Regional Dispatch Center records the approved alternative route and checks that the change does not leave a critical area without reasonable coverage.
S149: The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates destination consultation when a patient’s condition or the operating status of a facility may affect the assignment.
S150: The consultation uses the patient’s reported condition, transport estimate, and current facility acceptance information available to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S151: The Regional Medical Director provides clinical guidance when destination selection involves a specialized capability or a regional care protocol.
S152: The Hospital Liaison Desk contacts the Emergency Department to confirm whether the proposed destination can receive the patient.
S153: The Regional Dispatch Center uses the correction slip to reconcile a reported destination change with the active incident record.
S154: Larkspur confirms the incident identifier and intended receiving facility before the destination request is transmitted.
S155: The Emergency Department advises the Hospital Liaison Desk of relevant capacity limits, access constraints, or changes to its receiving status.
S156: The Hospital Liaison Desk records the consultation outcome and communicates any destination restriction to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S157: The Regional Dispatch Center evaluates the consultation outcome against patient acuity, transport time, and available ambulance coverage.
S158: The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents the approved destination and any associated operational instructions to dispatch staff.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
